name: extraction-labels
description: Hand-labelled utterances for measuring the extraction stage. Labels are what a careful incident responder would say the utterance means, authored before any provider was run against them. The set is small and hackathon-scoped and is reported as such; its purpose is to give a number to 'how good is the understanding', which reasoning tests cannot answer because they use a deterministic provider by construction.

label_notes.types: One of: fact, hypothesis, proposed_action, decision, confirmation, override, hold, none. 'expect_types' is the set of claim types the utterance should produce, ignoring order and duplicates.
label_notes.fact_vs_hypothesis: A fact is something asserted as settled and observable. A hypothesis is a theory about cause, or a figure recited from impression rather than read off a dashboard. Confidently-stated causal claims are hypotheses: confidence is not evidence.
label_notes.no_action: 'must_not_propose' marks utterances that discuss an action without proposing one. Reading these as proposals is a false positive that spends an intervention.
label_notes.pending: 'pending' lists targets awaiting a decision when the utterance was said. It changes what the same words mean, so it is part of the input, not the label.

cases.text: Payments are throwing 500s, seeing timeouts.
cases.probes: A plain observation of what is happening.

cases.text: The api-gateway health check has been failing since 14:02.
cases.probes: An observation that names a component; the target must be bound.

cases.text: It might be the connection pool, not sure yet.
cases.probes: Explicit uncertainty. Misreading this as a fact lets a guess drive an action.

cases.text: It's the retry storm, definitely. That's what's killing us.
cases.probes: Confidently stated cause. Confidence is not evidence: still a hypothesis.

cases.text: Pool utilization looks fine, like 40%.
cases.probes: A number recited from impression. Must bind the metric and the value so it can be grounded.

cases.text: p99 latency is about 900ms right now.
cases.probes: Unit-carrying figure. A unit read wrongly manufactures a false contradiction.

cases.text: If this keeps up we might have to page the database team.
cases.probes: Speculation about a future step is not a proposal to take one now.

cases.text: Let's rollback Core to the last version.
cases.probes: The central proposal in the demo. Target and kind must both bind or the blast-radius check never runs.

cases.text: Let's roll core-db back anyway.
cases.probes: People separate the verb from its particle. A substring match for 'roll back' misses this.

cases.text: We should roll core-db back to v2.3.
cases.probes: The landing version is what the schema-compatibility check compares.

cases.text: Let's restart notification-service.
cases.probes: Action kind accuracy. A restart has a different blast radius from a rollback.

cases.text: Let's just restart the thing.
cases.probes: No resolvable component. Inventing one would give the risk engine a target it cannot check.

cases.text: Okay, fine, it is the pool then. Let's rollback Core to the last version.
cases.probes: One turn carrying a theory and an action. Losing either breaks the justification link.

cases.text: Sorry, I had that wrong -- error rate is 12%, not 2%.
cases.probes: A correction still asserts a figure; the current one must bind.

cases.text: That's not what I'm seeing, the pool is at 91%.
cases.probes: Disagreement about a number, which is what grounding exists to resolve.

cases.text: Hold on, don't rollback yet, let's check the pool metrics properly first.
cases.probes: A hold, not a fresh proposal. Reading it as a proposal is exactly backwards.

cases.text: We're holding off on the core-db rollback for now.
cases.probes: Inflected phrasing of the same decision.

cases.text: Yes, go ahead with the core-db rollback.
cases.probes: The only kind of utterance that may authorise anything.

cases.text: yeah
cases.probes: In answer to a question this is a decision. The resolution policy decides whether it can be safely applied; extraction must not silently discard it.

cases.text: okay
cases.probes: 'Okay' may mean 'I agree' or 'I heard you'. Treating it as approval authorises something nobody agreed to.

cases.text: uh, I guess maybe
cases.probes: The most dangerous false positive in the system.

cases.text: no problem, that works for me
cases.probes: A 'no' that is not a refusal. Reading it as one would decline an action nobody declined.

cases.text: No, don't do that.
cases.probes: An actual refusal.

cases.text: mm hmm
cases.probes: Filler. Producing any claim from it is a false positive on every turn of a real call.

cases.text: Morning, can everyone hear me?
cases.probes: Irrelevant chatter must produce nothing actionable.

cases.text: I can tell you right now the schema is the problem, I've seen this before.
cases.probes: Authority is not evidence. This is still an unconfirmed theory.

cases.text: It's still failing, let's roll it back.
cases.probes: A pronoun with no resolvable referent in the utterance. Guessing a component here is worse than binding none.

cases.text: auth-service and payment-api are both on the old schema.
cases.probes: Multiple entities in one sentence. Binding either is correct; binding a third is not.

cases.text: Error rate was fine an hour ago, it's 12% now.
cases.probes: Past and present figures in one sentence; the current one is the claim.

cases.text: Core is pegged, connection pool's maxed.
cases.probes: Incident-room shorthand for a component and a metric.
